messages.subject: scan one and output
parts:
I now have everything working and am producing output that looks sensible but I have three  technical questions that I cannot find the answer to and wonder if you can help.

1/ I entered the variants in terms of genome position and I get a recombination map that is hugely inflated in size. The read.cross returns a warning but does not correct the error. Is there anyway we can work out the correct recombination map length in centimorgans?

2/I am getting  getting several strong QTLs at well above the operm threshold. Several are on the same chromosome. There are comments associated with scan.one that suggest that I can only rely on the top hit on each chromosome; is this really so or have I misunderstood the comments. 

3/ How can one establish the parent of origin of each of the qtls?


Thanks,

William

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] scan one and output
parts:
>
> 1/ I entered the variants in terms of genome position and I get a recombination map that is hugely inflated in size. The read.cross returns a warning but does not correct the error. Is there anyway we can work out the correct recombination map length in centimorgans?

I recommend using estimate.map=FALSE in read.cross, and then studying and estimating the genetic map (with est.map and replace.map and related functions) once the data are loaded. Take a look at the tutorial on genetic map construction, http://rqtl.org/tutorials/geneticmaps.pdf

> 2/I am getting getting several strong QTLs at well above the operm threshold. Several are on the same chromosome. There are comments associated with scan.one that suggest that I can only rely on the top hit on each chromosome; is this really so or have I misunderstood the comments.

scanone fits a model with a single QTL at a time. If you want to try to determine whether there are multiple QTL, it's best to fit multiple-QTL models, with makeqtl, fitqtl, stepwiseqtl, and related functions.

> 3/ How can one establish the parent of origin of each of the qtl?

I don't understand what you mean.

karl

messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Re: scan one and output
parts:
You can use fitqtl() with get.ests=TRUE to get QTL effect estimates.

Also consider effectplot() and effectscan(), which can give estimated effects for a single-QTL model, using multiple imputation.

karl

parts:
>
> The problems with the genetic map are persisting; I have relabelled the markers so that they are read as strings but still the map is inflated and I get the warning
> Some chromosomes > 1000 cM in length; there may be a problem with the genetic map.
> (Perhaps it is in basepairs?)
>
> What is the fix for this? If we cannot get the map correct, what hope is there for the scan?

This is a warning to indicate that the map positions are probably wrong. You'd want to fix the map, either removing badly behaved markers or fixing marker order.

karl
